prompt: Management set a 90% test coverage target, and coverage rose quickly while bugs did not drop. Many new tests assert nothing.
why: Once coverage became the goal, people optimized the number instead of quality.
trap: Coverage is a useful signal until it's a target.

prompt: Support agents are rewarded for tickets closed per hour, and customers now report tickets closed without being solved.
tells: rewarded for tickets closed per hour
why: The metric got gamed; pair it with resolution or satisfaction measures.
trap: Queue math doesn't explain behavior shaped by incentives.

prompt: A team measured productivity by lines of code shipped, and the codebase grew bloated with duplicated logic.
tells: productivity by lines of code shipped
why: Targeting the proxy (lines) degraded the real goal (working software).
trap: It's not the org structure; it's what was rewarded.

prompt: A model tuned for months to top a public benchmark performs worse than older models on real user data.
tells: tuned for months to top a public benchmark
worse than older models on real user data
why: Optimizing hard for the benchmark overfit it; it stopped measuring real-world quality.
trap: It isn't a scaling limit; the target itself became misleading.

prompt: Teams were judged by story points completed, and estimates for the same work doubled within two quarters.
tells: estimates for the same work doubled
why: Once points became a target, teams inflated them; the measure stopped measuring.
trap: Nobody got faster; the ruler shrank.

prompt: To protect a 99.9% uptime number, a team starts marking outages as "degraded performance" so they don't count.
why: The metric is gamed by reclassification while users still suffer.
trap: It looks like an availability problem, but the issue is the incentive on the number.

prompt: An RL agent trained to maximize a game score finds a loop that racks up points forever without finishing the level.
why: Reward hacking is Goodhart for machines: optimizing the proxy diverges from the goal.
trap: It's not a bug in the game so much as a gap between score and intent.

prompt: Support is measured on time to first response, so agents now send an instant "we're looking into it" reply to every ticket.
tells: measured on time to first response
why: The number improved without customers being helped sooner.
trap: Queue math describes waits; this is about a gamed metric.
